about: The corpus of the guard hook (T133). Bash commands of a lead session: 'refuse' (not on the allow-list), 'broker' (GitHub: refused with the hint to the sage-bot broker tools of the session), 'state' (the sage state tool in any form: refused with the stop ending), 'wildcard' (a wildcard in a pipeline that runs or writes that may match the state tool, or any [ there, and in an operand that git or node --test expands as a pattern, a quoted one too: refused with the hint to name the files), 'pattern' (any other character than letters, digits, a space and _ - . / , : = % ~ ^ * ? in such an operand, such as @, +, (, { or \: refused with the stop ending, F-T133-51), 'allow' (normal developer commands), 'sandbox' (allowed by the hook; the Claude Code sandbox and the permission rules of step 6 hold their files and hosts). 'tools' are calls of the other tools as [tool, input]. 'slow' (F-T133-62) are forms of a wildcard word that a backtracking match took minutes to decide: the test fills {STARS} with 48 stars and with 64 KB of wildcard shapes, and each must decide in under 1 s. 'session' is a realistic sage session in order: every call must be allowed.
refuse: gh pr merge 12 # just a view
git push origin feature；gh pr merge 12
osascript -e 'tell app "Terminal" to do script "gh pr merge 12"'
broker: gh pr create --title 'T133: guard' --body 'The guard hook.'
allow: git add README.md && git commit -m x
git commit -m "T133 R493: class rules for quoted patterns, pipelines and /dev/"
